questions.text: The lowest integer which is greater than 1 + 1/10^60 is........
questions.sol_text: 1 + 1/10^60 is a number slightly greater than 1. Since 1/10^60 is an extremely small positive number (essentially 0.000...001 with 60 zeros), 1 + 1/10^60 is just slightly more than 1. The lowest integer greater than this value is 2.

questions.text: Let S = {x ∈ [-6, 3] - {-2, 2} : (x + 3|-1) / (|x| - 2) ≥ 0}; and T = {x ∈ Z: x^2 - 7|x| + 9 ≤ 0}. Then the number of elements in S ∩ T is
questions.sol_text: For T: |x|^2 - 7|x| + 9 ≤ 0. Using quadratic formula, |x| ∈ [(7-sqrt(13))/2, (7+sqrt(13))/2]. Since 7-sqrt(13) ≈ 1.698 and 7+sqrt(13) ≈ 5.302, for x ∈ Z, x can be ±2, ±3, ±4, ±5. Among these, x = 3, -4, -5 satisfy S (after checking the rational inequality condition). Combining both conditions, n(S ∩ T) = 4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The number of integral solution x of log_{x+7/2}((x-7)/(2x-3))^2 ≥ 0 is:
questions.sol_text: Find domain: x + 7/2 > 0 and x + 7/2 ≠ 1 and (x-7)/(2x-3) ≠ 0. This gives x > -7/2, x ≠ -5/2, x ≠ 7, x ≠ 3/2. Case 1: When 0 < x + 7/2 < 1, i.e., -7/2 < x < -5/2, the inequality becomes ((x-7)/(2x-3))^2 ≤ 1, which gives -1 ≤ (x-7)/(2x-3) ≤ 1. Solving yields -7/2 < x < -5/2 (no integers). Case 2: When x + 7/2 > 1, i.e., x > -5/2, the inequality becomes ((x-7)/(2x-3))^2 ≥ 1, which gives (x-7)/(2x-3) ≤ -1 or (x-7)/(2x-3) ≥ 1. This gives x ∈ [-4, 3/2) ∪ (3/2, 10/3]. Combined with domain restrictions and x > -5/2: x ∈ (-5/2, 3/2) ∪ (3/2, 10/3]. The integers in this range are: -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3. Total = 6 integers.

questions.text:
The system of inequalities
a - b² ≥ 1/4, b - c² ≥ 1/4, c - d² ≥ 1/4,
d - a² ≥ 1/4 has
questions.sol_text:
Answer: (2)
Solution:
Answer (2)

a - b² ≥ 1/4

⇒ a ≥ b² + 1/4 ≥ 2b(1/2)
(AM ≥ G.M.)
⇒ a ≥ b

Hence the given system can be reduced to
a ≥ b, b ≥ c, c ≥ d, d ≥ a

Clearly a = b = c = d = 1/2

is the only possible solution.
